newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares up at noon on Lujiazui demand.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares up at noon on Lujiazui demand.

text.p: Shanghai B shares were modestly higher at midday on Friday as domestic institutions bought index heavyweight Shanghai Lujiazui Finance and Trade Zone Development, brokers said.
The B index put on 0.640 point or 0.88 percent to 73.543 on volume of 3.388 million shares worth $1.845 million, compared with $1.3 million on Thursday morning.
Brokers said follow-through buying could give the index a boost in the afternoon though they noted turnover has been thin of late with many foreign investors keeping to the sidelines.
"Institutional buying easily pushed the index up in today's thin market with most investors remaining cautious and looking for clearer direction," one broker said.

"Institutions may have been trying to boost investor confidence by buying index-weighted shares," another broker said. "They believe that the market should have a run in line with H-shares after the market showed signs of bottoming."
Of the 45 B share issues, 32 were traded with 20 of them gaining ground. Eight were lower and four unchanged.
Shanghai Lujiazui, the market bellwether, gained $0.026 or 2.10 percent to $1.260 on the back of institutional demand. It was the morning's most active issue on solid volume of 640,000 shares.
Huaxin Cement was the biggest gainer on technical buying as it rose $0.008 or 6.55 percent to $0.130 on volume of 48,000 shares.
Shanghai's A share index lost ground on a technical correction after gains over the past few days, brokers said.
The index shed 6.981 points or 0.56 percent to 1,238.594 on volume of 134.5 million shares worth 1.3 billion yuan.
The SSE30 blue chip index fell 34.835 points or 0.93 percent to 3,726.491 points.
Electrical equipment maker Xiamen Longzhou was the biggest loser on expectations of poor interim results. It tumbled 1.40 yuan or 8.23 percent to 15.60 yuan on volume of 618,100 shares.
